messages:
nate: Quick follow-up from the weights-loading RFC — hit a warmup-edge where per-shard quant profiles cause transient OOMs during streaming/hot-init. Repro below.

anita: Ugh. Can you paste the minimal repro + logs?

nate: Yep. Repro steps: streaming manifestless bundle, concurrent warmup of 2 shards, each arrives with different per-tensor scale tables. Loader applies dequant in-mem and we momentarily have both large dequant buffers + KV cache. Crash: OOM on allocation for dequant buffer.

nate: Log snippet:```
WARMUP INFO  loader: received shard s3://.../shard-2.bin
WARMUP DEBUG dequant: allocating 1.8GB dequant_buffer for shard-2 (table hash 0x9a3f)
WARMUP DEBUG dequant: allocating 1.6GB dequant_buffer for shard-3 (table hash 0xb7c2)
OOM Error: failed to allocate 1800000000 bytes
```

julia: Is this only when we fall back from quant->fp32 or when two different quant tables are in-memory simultaneously?

nate: It's the latter. Streaming fetch means shards can be hydrated in parallel on the same host. If their quant metadata differs, we currently allocate separate dequant buffers rather than reusing or streaming-dequant. So peak memory is sum of both.

kevin: I thought the invariant was: "bundle-level canonical quant table". Are manifestless/legacy bundles violating that?

nate: Manifestless bundles frequently come from older export pipelines that emit per-shard quant profiles. Newer bundle tooling usually normalizes at bundle level. The loader can't assume normalisation for manifestless streams.

anita: Options I see: 1) Enforce canonical quant table at ingest (strong but breaks old exports). 2) Merge quant tables at upload (transcode) — costy. 3) At runtime, detect mismatch and switch to streaming dequant (memory-mapped, chunked dequant) to reduce peak. 4) Backpressure warmup (serialise shard warmup) so only one big dequant buffer at a time.

julia: Tradeoffs: (1) simplest for runtime but customer-facing; (3) safest for compatibility with performance hit. (4) might increase tail latency for first requests.

nate: Proposed pragmatic plan:
- Short-term: implement runtime detection + streaming dequant fallback. This reduces peak memory with modest perf cost. Add a telemetry counter quant_mismatch_fallback_count.
- Medium: add loader API field quant_profile_hash in the shard manifest/headers so routing can avoid co-locating incompatible shards when possible.
- Long-term: encourage bundle canonicalization on upload; provide a transcode tool that auto-normalizes quant tables (opt-in).

anita: I like short-term fallback + telemetry. Also need an infra metric / alert if fallback rate > X per hour.

kevin: For the loader API addition, we should avoid breaking wire format. Add optional header: `X-Quant-Hash` and expose in weightsource metadata. Downstream routing can use it.

nate: I'll draft the small RFC addendum listing the loader changes, fallback algorithm pseudo-code, and the repro. Pseudo:```
if shard.quant_hash != bundle.quant_hash:
    if memory_headroom < dequant_estimate:
        use_streaming_dequant(shard)
    else:
        allocate_dequant(shard)
```

anita: I'll own telemetry + dashboards (assigning myself). Will add `quant_mismatch_fallback_count`, `quant_mismatch_per_host`, and OOM correlate graph.

infra-bot: created issue eng-ml#987: "quant-profile mismatch during warmup - mitigation proposals" (link: https://redwood.internal/eng-ml/issues/987) :white_check_mark:

julia: I'll draft the RFC addendum and push a short PR for header spec. Nate will own unit/integration tests for the fallback path. Anita will own metrics/dashboards.

kevin: Quick sync tomorrow 10:00 to align on rollout plan. Anyone can't make it?

nate: I can. I'll post repro artifacts in the issue.

anita: 👍 I'll include a sample dashboard and alert thresholds in the issue.

julia: Thanks all — will ping when RFC addendum is ready for review.
